ops.title: viz trailer collection: no range fallback on a truncated walk window
ops.body:
`reachFrom` (internal/viz/commits.go) records `rs.root` only when a parentless commit appears within the `maxCommitLimit` (1000) walk window. On history deeper than the window, or a shallow clone whose deepest fetched commit still names a missing parent, `rs.root` stays empty. It previously flowed straight into `git show -s --format=%(trailers:key=cc-task,valueonly) ""`, 500ing every `/api/commits` request (hit once local repos crossed 1000 commits).

The tempting fix — bound the range at the oldest walked commit — is wrong twice, and both failure modes are now pinned by tests:

1. **Lossy under clock skew.** `WalkCommits` pops newest-first by committer time, so the last-popped commit is NOT guaranteed to be free of walked ancestors. A merge whose parents are older than their own shared ancestor walks as [m, a, r, b]: bounding at `b` drops `r`'s trailers even though `r` is displayed on the page. Pinned by `TestCommitsSkewedMergeShallowTrailers`.
2. **Unbounded cost.** `git log <oldest>..<tip>` traverses everything reachable from tip but not from oldest — on a merge with a huge left arm that is the entire arm, so `maxCommitLimit` stops bounding subprocess output.

Instead the truncated branch reads the walked set verbatim via `gitcmd.TaskTrailersAt` — `git log --stdin --no-walk=unsorted` over exactly the walked shas. No range semantics, no traversal, cost linear in the window. `--no-walk` is load-bearing and pinned by an unrequested trailer-carrying ancestor in `TestTaskTrailersAt`; without the flag that ancestor leaks into the map.

Both root-bearing paths (fork..tip for forked lanes, root..tip plus the root's own trailers for trunk) are unchanged.
